    Applications

    Applications by sector

    Where our ingredients are used, drawn from the catalogue. Each product is listed under the sectors its specification supports.

    01

    Nutraceuticals & dietary supplements

    Standardized extracts specified by marker compound, for capsule, tablet, powder and softgel formats.

    • GingerZingiber officinale

      Digestive comfort and nausea-relief, the largest use category.

    • TurmericCurcuma longa

      Standardized curcuminoid extract, often paired with a bioavailability enhancer.

    • PepperPiper nigrum

      Standardized piperine extract to improve absorption of other actives in a formulation.

    • CinnamonCinnamomum verum / cassia

      Standardized extract in metabolic-wellness formulations.

    • Garcinia CambogiaGarcinia gummi-gutta

      The primary category, almost always as a standardized calcium/potassium salt.

    • Green CoffeeCoffea arabica / robusta

      The dominant use case for standardized CGA extract.

    • Green TeaCamellia sinensis

      The largest category for standardized polyphenol/EGCG extract.

    • AshwagandhaWithania somnifera

      The leading category: stress, sleep, and vitality supplements.

      Recovery and strength-support formulations.

    • Tulsi (Holy Basil)Ocimum tenuiflorum

      Adaptogenic stress and immune-support, often positioned alongside ashwagandha.

    • Boswellia SerrataBoswellia serrata

      Joint-comfort and mobility-support, the dominant category.

    • BacopaBacopa monnieri

      Cognitive-support and nootropic formulations, the primary use case.

      Focus-support products for sustained mental performance.

    02

    Food, beverage & functional foods

    Oleoresins, CO₂ extracts and essential oils for consistent flavor and color; functional extracts for fortified foods and drinks.

    • GingerZingiber officinale

      Ginger ale, confectionery, and spice blends use the oleoresin or CO2 oil for consistent flavor.

    • TurmericCurcuma longa

      Natural yellow-orange colorant, standardized separately from the health-focused extract grade.

    • PepperPiper nigrum

      Oleoresin and essential oil replace ground pepper where consistency matters.

    • CinnamonCinnamomum verum / cassia

      Baking, beverage, and confectionery flavoring.

    • NutmegMyristica fragrans

      Baking, beverage, and spice-blend flavoring, the dominant application.

    • Garcinia CambogiaGarcinia gummi-gutta

      Metabolic-support drinks, where the water-soluble salt dissolves cleanly.

    • Green CoffeeCoffea arabica / robusta

      Chlorogenic-acid-rich unroasted bean extract, with caffeinated and decaffeinated grades available.

    • Green TeaCamellia sinensis

      Unfermented-leaf extract standardized to total polyphenols or specific EGCG content.

    • AshwagandhaWithania somnifera

      Root-only adaptogen extract standardized on withanolide content, a leading category in global supplements.

    • Tulsi (Holy Basil)Ocimum tenuiflorum

      Tulsi tea is one of the largest single applications for this leaf extract.

    • BacopaBacopa monnieri

      Bacoside-standardized whole-herb extract, an anchor ingredient in nootropic formulations.

    03

    Pharmaceuticals

    Botanical extracts used in pharmaceutical formulation, and acetophenones used as pharmaceutical intermediates.

    • GingerZingiber officinale

      CO2 and solvent extracts standardized on gingerols, shogaols, and zingiberene.

    • TurmericCurcuma longa

      Curcuminoid-standardized extract and oleoresin, valued as both a functional ingredient and a natural colorant.

    • Boswellia SerrataBoswellia serrata

      Gum resin extract standardized on boswellic acids, the established botanical in the joint-comfort category.

    3 aroma chemicals4-Methylacetophenone, 4-Bromoacetophenone, 4-Methoxyacetophenone Register with CAS numbers

    04

    Cosmetics & personal care

    Botanical extracts and oils used in skincare formulation.

    • TurmericCurcuma longa

      Curcuminoid-standardized extract and oleoresin, valued as both a functional ingredient and a natural colorant.

    • NutmegMyristica fragrans

      Myristicin-carrying seed oil and oleoresin prized for a warm aromatic profile in flavor and fragrance work.

    • Green CoffeeCoffea arabica / robusta

      Green coffee oil (the bean's lipid fraction) in eye-care and firming skincare.

    • Green TeaCamellia sinensis

      EGCG's antioxidant profile in anti-aging and soothing skincare.

    05

    Fragrance & flavor

    Aliphatic ketones and acetophenones used as aroma chemicals, alongside spice essential oils.

    • NutmegMyristica fragrans

      The essential oil's warm, woody-spicy note in fine fragrance work.

    • Boswellia SerrataBoswellia serrata

      The essential oil is a well-established frankincense note, independent of the extract's functional use.
